text: The subject Tariq Nawaz holds account PK**MUCB****4062 opened on 6 July 2024. The subject is declared as a Student with a declared monthly income of PKR 25,000 per month. During the activity window from 2 April 2026 to 10 April 2026 the account recorded 17 credits totalling PKR 932,000 and 4 debits totalling PKR 875,000. The credits arrived via 17 interbank (IBFT) transfers from 13 distinct senders. The activity was flagged by Tazama on 10 April 2026, with the typology MULE-01 scoring 360 against a threshold of 300. The presence of 13 distinct inbound senders in a short period aligns with the many unrelated inbound senders indicator. Debits equal to 94% of credits and a median of 4.5 hours between the latest credit and each debit suggest that most inbound value leaves the account within hours. Credits in the activity window were 37.3 times the declared monthly income, which is inconsistent with the subject’s declared occupation as a Student and declared income of PKR 25,000 per month. Two sender banks raised fraud recall requests against inbound transfers to this account, indicating potential fraud concerns. Overall, the pattern is consistent with suspected money mule activity given the many senders, rapid outflow, and mismatch with the subject’s Student occupation and PKR 25,000 per month income. PKR 642,000 was sent to QuickPay wallet ***0932 (WLT****0932, Synthetic EMI) in 3 transactions. PKR 233,000 was withdrawn as Cash (ATM) in 1 transaction. Screening on 28 April 2026 found no match on sanctions, PEP or adverse-media lists. Outgoing wallet transfers were placed on hold pending review, with no contact made with the customer about this review.
